correctness.rationale: Strict finite-\(n\) optimality follows from an exact second-derivative identity for a Gaussian interval mass and binomial symmetry. The asymptotic coefficients follow from explicit Taylor expansions, exact standardized binomial moments through order six, Stirling expansion, and exponentially small tail control. The included exact-sum checker reproduces the predicted scaled constants; it is not used as proof of the infinite statement.

value.rationale: The quantization convention is part of the definition of the discrete entropic CLT. In the canonical symmetric Bernoulli model, changing from boundary-aligned to midpoint cells removes the entire leading KL term, improving the convergence order from \(n^{-1}\) to \(n^{-2}\). This is a structural continuity-correction effect rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
